blind_vlm_explanation: This is a classic chloride-dominated Type 3 grain (3-Cl, identical in morphology to Reference 5). It exhibits a strong Na+(NaCl) peak near 81-83 u (prom=0.292), a mixed chloride-hydroxide peak centered at 122.0 u, and a Na+(NaCl)2 / Na+(NaOH)3 peak at 139-143 u, while the diagnostic orthophosphate bands at 165 u and 187 u are completely flat and devoid of resolved positive peaks.

The candidate spectrum (SCLK 1511748839) displays a clean Type 3 salt-rich backbone with well-resolved Na+ (23 u) and Na+(NaOH) (63 u, prominence 0.322) peaks and no water-cluster comb or chloride dominance. In the zoomed 70-195 u diagnostic window, all three members of the sodium orthophosphate triplet are clearly resolved above the local continuum: Na+(NaPO3) at ~126.5 u (prominence 0.143, diff_125_minus_129 = +0.0182), a strong Na+(Na2HPO4) peak at ~166.5 u (prominence 0.186), and a prominent Na+(Na3PO4) peak at ~189.5 u (prominence 0.256). This unambiguously confirms a genuine 3-P phosphate-bearing grain.

The candidate spectrum (SCLK 1509344418) exhibits a clear Type 3 salt-rich backbone with strong Na+ (23 u) and Na+(NaOH) (63 u) peaks and no interfering water-cluster comb or chloride (81 u, 139 u) dominance. In the zoomed anion diagnostic window (70-195 u), the spectrum displays the complete, resolved orthophosphate peak sequence corresponding to Na+(NaPO3) around 125-127 u (prominence 0.101), Na+(Na2HPO4) around 165-168 u (prominence 0.100), and Na+(Na3PO4) around 187-192 u (prominence 0.148), along with the characteristic companion feature near 108-110 u seen in Reference 1 and Reference 2. The slight +2 to +3 u shift at the highest masses is a minor calibration stretch artifact where the stretch parameter hit the lower bound (a = 0.4620 us/sqrt(u)) due to the broad 23 u peak profile. All three diagnostic orthophosphate peaks are clearly resolved above the local continuum, confirming a genuine '3-P' grain.

Therefore, it is classified as non-3-P.
